title: Canada Caregiver Visa 2026: Requirements, NOC & PR Route
metaDescription: Canada caregiver visa 2026: Home Care Worker pilots, CLB 4 language, six months experience, NOC 44100 and 44101, job offer rules and paused intake explained.
headline: Canada Caregiver Visa 2026: Requirements and PR Route

sections.title: Canada's Home Care Worker Immigration Pilots
sections.content:
Canada's Home Care Worker Immigration Pilots offer a direct route to permanent residence for caregivers working in private homes or home-care organisations. The two streams cover child care, under NOC 44100, and home support for seniors and people with disabilities, under NOC 44101, with nurse aides in home care also recognised in some cases.

Applicants should note that intake under these pilots was paused in December 2025, with a redesigned caregiver programme signalled for late 2026. Anyone planning an application should verify the current intake status on the official IRCC website before paying fees or resigning from a job.

sections.title: Language, Education and Experience Requirements
sections.content:
Applicants need language ability at Canadian Language Benchmark 4 in all four skills, proven by an approved English or French test such as IELTS General, CELPIP, TEF Canada or TCF Canada. Education must equal a Canadian high school diploma, with foreign credentials assessed through an Educational Credential Assessment.

Work experience or training must be recent and relevant: six months of paid work in NOC 44100 or 44101, or a six-month relevant training credential, within the past three years. Informal unpaid family caregiving generally does not count unless it was verifiable paid employment with proper records.

sections.title: Job Offer and Employer Rules
sections.content:
A qualifying job offer must be full-time, at least 30 hours per week, from an eligible employer outside Quebec, either a private household or a home-care organisation that directly employs the caregiver. Third-party placement agencies that do not employ the caregiver do not qualify, and the employer must have operated in Canada for at least one year.

The offer must use the IRCC-prescribed employment form, state the correct NOC, wage and duties, and comply with provincial labour standards. Care duties must be genuine: household chores alone do not qualify, and the role must centre on direct care such as supervision, personal care and mobility support.

sections.title: Application Steps, Fees and Common Refusals
sections.content:
Applications are submitted online through the IRCC Permanent Residence Portal with the passport, language results, credential assessment, reference letters, police certificates and medical results. The principal applicant processing fee is CAD 990 plus an CAD 85 biometrics fee, with a right of permanent residence fee payable before the final decision.

Common refusals come from fake or informal job offers, the wrong NOC code, undocumented experience and expired language tests. Because misrepresentation can bring a five-year ban, applicants should use only licensed immigration consultants and never surrender a passport to an employer or agent.

faqs.q: What language level is needed for a Canada caregiver visa?
faqs.a: The Home Care Worker pilots require Canadian Language Benchmark 4 in listening, speaking, reading and writing, proven by an approved test such as IELTS General, CELPIP, TEF Canada or TCF Canada. A higher score does not improve odds because the programme is not points-based, but booking the test early matters because seats fill quickly.

faqs.q: How much caregiver experience do I need for Canada?
faqs.a: You need six months of recent, relevant paid experience in NOC 44100 or 44101, or a six-month relevant training credential, gained within the past three years. Experience must be documented with reference letters and pay records, because informal unpaid family caregiving generally does not satisfy the requirement on its own.

faqs.q: Which caregiver jobs qualify for Canadian immigration?
faqs.a: Qualifying roles are home child care providers under NOC 44100 and home support workers under NOC 44101, plus nurse aides in home-care settings in some cases. The work must involve direct care in a private home or home-care organisation, while housekeeping duties alone and hospital or long-term care roles fall outside these streams.

faqs.q: Are Canada caregiver pilots open in 2026?
faqs.a: Intake under the Home Care Worker pilots was paused in December 2025, and IRCC has signalled a redesigned caregiver programme for late 2026. Applicants should check the official IRCC website for reopening dates and caps before applying, and should beware of agents selling places in a programme that is currently closed.
